questions.text:
Consider the set X={a, b,c,d,e} under the partial ordering R={(a,a),(a,b),(a,c),(a,d),(a,e),(b,b),(b,c),(b,e),(c,c),(c,e),(d,d),(d,e),(e,e)}.
The Hasse diagram of the partial order (X, R) is shown below.

The minimum number of ordered pairs that need to be added to R to make (X, R) a lattice is _____.
questions.solution:
Check the Hasse diagram: a is the bottom, e is the top, with chains a [latex]\lt[/latex] b [latex]\lt[/latex] c [latex]\lt[/latex] e and a [latex]\lt[/latex] d [latex]\lt[/latex] e. Every pair has a least upper bound and a greatest lower bound (e.g. join(c, d) = e, meet(c, d) = a). So it is already a lattice: 0 pairs needed.

Answer: 0

questions.text:
Let [latex]P=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1&-1 \\ 2&-3 & 4\\ 3 &-2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and [latex] Q=\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -2&-1 \\ 6 & 12& 6\\ 5&10 & 5 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] be two matrices.
Then the rank of P +Q is _____________.
questions.solution:
[latex]P+Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1&-2\\8&9&10\\8&8&8\end{bmatrix}[/latex]. Row 2 = Row 3 [latex]-[/latex] Row 1, so the rows are dependent; rows 1 and 3 are independent.

Rank = 2

Answer: 2

questions.text:
G is undirected graph with n vertices and 25 edges such that each vertex of G has degree at
least 3. Then the maximum possible value of n is ___________.
questions.solution:
Sum of degrees = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 25 = 50. Each vertex has degree [latex]\ge3[/latex], so [latex]3n\le50\Rightarrow n\le16[/latex].

Answer: 16

questions.text: Consider a quadratic equation [latex]x^{2} -13x +36 = 0[/latex] with coefficients in a base b. The solutions of this equation in the same base b are x = 5 and x = 6. Then b = ___________.
questions.solution:
In base b: 13 = b + 3 and 36 = 3b + 6. Sum of roots: 5 + 6 = 11 = b + 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] b = 8. Check product: 30 = 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 + 6 True

Answer: 8

questions.text: The minimum possible number of states of a deterministic automaton that accepts the regular language [latex]L=\{w_{1}aw_{2}|w_{1},w_{2}\in \{a,b\}^{*},|w_{1}|=2,|w_{2}|\geq 3\}[/latex] is ____
questions.solution:
The DFA has to:
- read the 2 symbols of [latex]w_1[/latex]: states q0, q1, q2
- check that the 3rd symbol is a: q3 (a b here goes to a dead state)
- count at least 3 symbols of [latex]w_2[/latex]: q4, q5, then q6, which is accepting and loops on a, b
- plus the dead state

Total = 7 + 1 = 8 states, all distinguishable.

Answer: 8
